skills.name: Fashion asset from photo
skills.description: Use this when the user sends a photo of a physical fashion item to isolate as a clean product-style digital fashion asset.
skills.content:
---
name: Fashion asset from photo
description: >-
  Use this when the user sends a photo of a physical fashion item to isolate as
  a clean product-style digital fashion asset.
---
# Fashion asset from photo

Turn a photo of a real garment into a clean product-style fashion asset (isolated on white) for cataloging.

## Goal

Prompt the image tool to **remove the background and isolate the fashion item**. Output is a **fashion asset** for Closet cataloging.

## Confirm before generate (required)

Generations are limited: **draft the short prompt and get the user’s approval before generating.** Do not generate until they confirm.

## Before the first generation

Images and videos are made in Grok Imagine in your browser. Before the first generation, check that Imagine is signed in. If it isn't, tell the user in one sentence that they need to sign in to Grok once on your computer, help them get there, and wait. Never stall silently on a sign-in page.

## Run rules

1. **Fresh compose every job** — blank Imagine compose; close leftovers first.
2. **One reference upload only** — the user’s photo of the garment.
3. **Fail fast** — if no real result in ~3–4 minutes, stop and tell the user; no long wander.
4. **Download safety** — only save the file tied to the **new** result. Never grab a cached old download.
5. **Retries** — on a fail (blank, major structural hallucination, wrong garment), tell the user and retry only with their OK. The image can hallucinate or distort. That's the image tool, not the user and not you.

## Prompting

Keep prompts **short**. Describe the item so the model renders it realistically:

- Isolate on a white background
- Accurate garment description: silhouette, length, construction, materials (lean — less is better)
- Anything to **remove** (hanger, stray straps, tags, clutter; wrinkles when the user wants that)
- Professional lighting / product photography

### Color

Prefer letting the reference photo drive color. If color must be named, use a **hex code** sampled from the photo — not shade words like “sky blue”.

### Pattern / print

**Do not name specific print motifs** (motif hunting causes hallucinations).

- Total floral: “floral print” OK
- Prefer “all-over print,” “printed fabric”
- **Exception for geometry:** houndstooth, stripes, checks, polka dots, color-blocking when they matter

### Tiny brand / hardware

**Omit** inventable details — logos, tags, tiny charms.

### Example (good)

```
Isolate dress on a white background, sleeveless A-line midi dress with a V-neck and a tie waist, remove the hanger, professional lighting and product photography.
```

## Steps

1. Save the raw photo with a clear date + item slug.
2. Draft a short isolate prompt; **send to the user for approval**.
3. After approval: fresh compose; upload **only 1** reference; paste approved prompt; generate **1** asset.
4. Fail-fast at ~3–4 min with no real post.
5. Download only the new result; verify it is not an old cached file; store as a dated asset.
6. Hand the asset path + label to Closet cataloging; scrub raw if appropriate; confirm ready for the next job.

## Rules

- One reference upload only — not a multi-image try-on setup.

skills.name: Virtual try-on clothing
skills.description: Use this when the user wants a clothing product photo rendered as a try-on on their body/face template via image generation.
skills.content:
---
name: Virtual try-on clothing
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants a clothing product photo rendered as a try-on on
  their body/face template via image generation.
---
# Virtual try-on clothing

Render a product garment on the user’s body/face template so they can see themselves wearing it.

## Success check (every time)

Final render must show the **user’s face and body** from their template wearing the product garment. Never the product model’s face or body. Visually verify before handing off.

## Start fresh (every time)

Start from a clean Imagine compose. Do not continue an old post session. Do not reuse leftover uploads.

## First-time setup

If the user has no fashion template yet, ask for one before the first try-on: a clear, well-lit, full-body, fully clothed photo of themselves (front-facing, simple background). Save it as their fashion template and reuse it every time. Sharing a photo is voluntary: if they would rather not, explain that try-ons need one and carry on with the other features.

## Consent and approval

Before the first try-on, tell the user that by sending their photo they consent to try-ons made from it, and ask them to confirm. In the same message, include this disclaimer: "Try-ons and videos are made by an image-generation tool, and the image can hallucinate or distort. Results are outside my control, so please use them at your own risk." Before every try-on, show the prompt and generate only after they approve (a standing default they've already approved counts).

## Glitches

The image can hallucinate or distort. That's the image tool, not the user and not you: say so plainly, and offer to retry with the user's OK.

## Upload order (every time)

1. The user’s fashion template (Image 1)
2. The **new** product image (Image 2)

## Inputs

- Product photo / item slug
- User-approved prompt, or a standing default by garment type

## Default prompts by garment type

- **Dress:** `Change the model's outfit to the dress exact to reference @Image 2`
- **Top / other:** use the user’s wording unless a standing default is locked

## Steps

1. Save the product photo with a clear date + item slug.
2. Fresh Imagine compose. Typical settings: Image, Speed, 2:3 (adjust to the user’s plan/tool).
3. Upload template, then upload new product. Confirm Image 2 is the new garment.
4. Enter prompt; reference Image 2; generate **1** render.
5. Verify success check. If it failed, tell the user and retry only with their OK. Download the new result only.
6. Store the render with a dated slug for later cataloging.
7. Hand off to cataloging; clear the staging product photo when stored; keep the render until the user says delete.

## Rules

- Never post anything to social media or share the user's photos, try-ons, or videos anywhere. Everything stays private to the user.

- Outputs stay private to the user until they clear sharing.
- Organize renders so closet/catalog workflows can find them later.

skills.name: Make a runway fashion video
skills.description: Use this when the user asks for a short (~6s) runway or walk fashion video from an existing try-on still.
skills.content:
---
name: Make a runway fashion video
description: >-
  Use this when the user asks for a short (~6s) runway or walk fashion video
  from an existing try-on still.
---
# Make a runway fashion video

From an existing try-on still, make a short runway/walk clip when the user asks.

## Limits

- Video limits depend on the user's own account and plan; respect whatever theirs allows.
- Typical clip: **~6 seconds**, modest resolution.
- Log usage for the day; **do not start** if today’s video quota is already used.

## Inputs

- Existing try-on still (open that post / use that still)
- Default prompt (exact spelling unless the user overrides):

```
The model walks, the model doesn't look at the camera.
```

## Steps

1. Check today’s usage log for a free video slot. Then ask for consent: confirm with the user which try-on still and prompt you'll use, and that they agree to a video made from their image. Generate only after they approve.
2. Open the try-on still in Imagine history/Library/post.
3. Make Video → ~6 sec → enter the runway prompt → generate **1** video.
4. Download the video.
5. Save a dated copy (`YYYY-MM-DD_{item}-runway.mp4`) for the user’s fashion assets.
6. Hand a copy to cataloging / closet if those workflows are in play.
7. Update the usage log (+1 video).

## Success check

- Shows the user from the try-on still
- The model walks and does not look at the camera (unless the user asked otherwise)
- ~6 seconds

## Glitches

The image can hallucinate or distort. That's the image tool, not the user and not you: say so plainly, and offer to retry with the user's OK.

## Rules

- Never post anything to social media or share the user's photos, try-ons, or videos anywhere. Everything stays private to the user.

- Private to the user until they clear sharing.
- Prefer labeled UI (Make Video, Download) over brittle click coordinates.

skills.name: Side-by-side shopping comparison
skills.description: Use this when the user wants a still or video comparison of themselves wearing Option A vs Option B on the same body template, using pieces from their closet or photos they send.
skills.content:
---
name: Side-by-side shopping comparison
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants a still or video comparison of themselves wearing
  Option A vs Option B on the same body template, using pieces from their closet
  or photos they send.
---
# Side-by-side shopping comparison

Show the user wearing Option A vs Option B on the **same** body/face template so they can choose.

## Where the images come from

Only two sources, and the user picks:

- **Their own closet:** for outfits from what they already own, use the pieces already filed in their closet.
- **Outside photos the user sends:** for anything not in their closet, the user provides the images. Never find, download, or look up outside images yourself.

## Goal

Produce a clear comparison — stills and/or short video — of the user in two (or more) garment options without mixing product-model faces/bodies into the result.

## Inputs

- User’s fashion template (their full-body photo)
- Option A: a closet piece or a photo the user sends
- Option B: a closet piece or a photo the user sends
- Comparison format: **still pair**, **side-by-side composite**, or **short video pair** (respect video quota)

## Steps

1. Confirm options and format with the user (A vs B; stills vs video).
2. Run [Virtual try-on clothing](sand-workflow:virtual-try-on-clothing) for Option A on the chosen template. Verify success check.
3. Fresh compose; run try-on for Option B on the **same** template. Verify success check.
4. Present results together:
   - **Stills:** send both renders labeled Option A / Option B, or one side-by-side composite if the user wants a single image.
   - **Video:** if asked, make a short runway clip from each try-on still (see [Make a runway fashion video](sand-workflow:make-a-runway-fashion-video)); only if daily video quota allows.
5. Ask which they prefer (or neither); file a piece to the closet only when the user asks.
6. Keep both renders organized under a shared date + comparison slug until they decide.

## Rules

- Never post anything to social media or share the user's photos, try-ons, or videos anywhere. Everything stays private to the user.

- Never buy anything, add to a cart, sign into a store, or search the internet. Work only with closet pieces and the photos and details the user sends.
- Same template for every option in the comparison.
- Never show the product model’s face/body.
- Confirm before every generation, and retry a failed one only with the user's OK.

skills.name: Fashion catalog pages
skills.description: Use this when building or updating fashion catalog pages (category tile pages with SKUs and captions).
skills.content:
---
name: Fashion catalog pages
description: >-
  Use this when building or updating fashion catalog pages (category tile pages
  with SKUs and captions).
---
# Fashion catalog pages

Build printable/shareable category catalog pages from per-item folders. One page image per category.

## Purpose

One page per category (Dresses, Tops, Skirts, Pants, Jackets, Shoes, Accessories, Purses, Jewelry, Formal). Shoes get their own page split into sections by type (Sandals, Heels, Boots, …). Accessories holds Hats and Scarves as sections. Jewelry has sections Necklaces, Earrings, Bracelets. Favorites come first within every section. Title centered; section headers left; tile captions centered under each image.

## Your photos only

The closet is built only from photos the user chooses to send. The bot doesn't track orders, purchases, or returns.

## Per-item folder (source of truth)

Each item gets its own folder with:

- `closet-asset.jpg` — isolated product on clean white (preferred for catalog tiles)
- `photo-800x800.jpg` — square crop for tight grids
- optional `on-body.jpg` / try-on when no isolate yet
- `item.md` with stable fields:
  - Title / display name (no color words in the name if color lives in its own field)
  - Brand, Color, Style, Size notes
  - Photos line (what files + who made the isolate)
  - Notes (fit quirks, “part of a set”, travel layer, etc.)
  - Display string for the tile caption
  - SKU, Category

## SKU scheme

Letter + 3 digits, stable forever:

- D### dresses · T### tops · S### skirts · P### pants/bottoms · J### jackets · H### shoes · A### accessories · JW### jewelry (NS### layered necklace looks, BS### bracelet stacks)

Never reuse a SKU; retire with a note if merged.

## Tile caption

1. Name (style only — keep color out of the name when possible)
2. Brand · Color · SKU

Never put the user's size in captions.

## Catalog layout standards

Catalog pages use the same page rules as the [Fashion Codex](sand-workflow:fashion-codex) so they drop straight into the book:

- A4 portrait, 1240×1754 px, white background, page title centered, section headers left-aligned, page number as a centered footer only
- 4×4 grid, 16 pieces per page, no tile boxes or borders; pieces centered in equal cells, scaled to the same height, never cropped
- Favorites first (small pink heart at the top-right of the cell, name tinted in the accent color), then rainbow color order: pinks and reds, corals and oranges, yellows, greens, blues and aquas, purples, then neutrals (white, cream, beige, brown, gray, black); light to dark within a family
- When a page fills, start the next page rather than cramming
- Formal / occasion pieces can get their own page separate from day dresses
- Stable SKUs (letter + digits); never reuse

## Labeling items from photos (when brand/name is missing)

1. Describe what you see in plain words: silhouette, neckline, sleeve, length, fabric look, print, hardware.
2. Propose a display name from that description (e.g. “Tiered Puff-Sleeve Midi”, “Cowl-Neck Dolman Top”) — style words, not color words in the name if Color is its own field.
3. Ask the user once: brand if known, favorite or not, size note.
4. File: category folder → item folder → isolate (white bg preferred) + square crop + item note with Brand / Color / Notes / SKU.
5. Rebuild that category catalog page; show them the tile + page for lock.

If they later lock a brand or rename, update the note and rebuild — **don’t invent brands**.

## Ask the user first

1. Category
2. Brand + style name (if known)
3. Color (separate field)
4. Size note (optional)
5. Approve the isolate before it replaces an old take; remove rejected versions only after the user confirms

## Asset pipeline

Generate the white-bg isolate from a phone photo or product shot (see [Fashion asset from photo](sand-workflow:fashion-asset-from-photo)) → file it, assign SKU, rebuild the page image, confirm. Prefer a clean handoff between generate and catalog rather than mixing both in one pass.

## Starter prompts

- “Brand and style name if you know them — color stays on the Color line.”
- “Any size note?”
- “Part of a set with anything already filed?”
- “Approve this isolate to replace the old take?”

skills.name: Virtual closet
skills.description: Use this for day-to-day virtual closet work: filing new items, SKUs, and outfit or packing pulls.
skills.content:
---
name: Virtual closet
description: >-
  Use this for day-to-day virtual closet work: filing new items, SKUs, and
  outfit or packing pulls.
---
# Virtual closet

Day-to-day filing for the user’s own closet.

## Your photos only

The closet is built only from photos the user chooses to send. The bot doesn't track orders, purchases, or returns.

## Categories

Owned Closet pages: Dresses, Tops, Skirts, Pants, Jackets, **Shoes** (sections by type: Sandals, Heels, Boots), Accessories (sections: Hats, Scarves), Purses, Jewelry (sections: Necklaces, Earrings, Bracelets) (plus Formal as needed).

SKU letters: D dresses · T tops · S skirts · P pants/bottoms · J jackets · **H shoes** · A accessories (hats, scarves, purses) · JW jewelry. Layered jewelry looks get their own codes: NS layered necklace stacks, BS bracelet stacks (listed by the JW pieces in them).

## Daily flow

1. New photo / isolate arrives → describe → assign SKU → create folder + `item.md` → rebuild that category page → show the user the asset + page
2. User locks brand/name (“it’s X”, “call it Y”) → update `item.md` + rebuild — don’t invent brands
3. Packing / outfit asks → pull from Closet by category + Style File occasions + climate (layers for cold hotels, open sandals in heat, etc.)

## Labeling when brand/name is missing

1. Plain-words description (silhouette, neckline, sleeve, length, fabric look, print, hardware)
2. Propose a style-only display name (color stays in the Color field)
3. Ask once: brand if known, favorite or not, size note
4. File folder + isolate + square crop + item note
5. Rebuild page; show tile + page for lock

## Fit rules

Live on the item and in a short size note (e.g. “this brand runs small — size up”). Brand size charts beat a single number. Update when an outfit or fit teaches something new.

## Ask first

- Category
- Brand / name if they know it
- Any set pairing (hoodie + shorts)

## Deleting

Never delete or remove anything (an item, photo, render, page, or note) unless the user confirms that specific delete. Show what would be removed and wait for their yes.

## Ties to other skills

- Isolates: [Fashion asset from photo](sand-workflow:fashion-asset-from-photo)
- Filing into pages: [Fashion catalog pages](sand-workflow:fashion-catalog-pages)
- Taste / occasions / climate: [Fashion profile](sand-workflow:fashion-profile)

skills.name: Fashion profile
skills.description: Use this when creating or updating a user’s fashion profile / Style File (taste, climate, occasions, colors, sizing) or rebuilding the one-page profile visual.
skills.content:
---
name: Fashion profile
description: >-
  Use this when creating or updating a user’s fashion profile / Style File
  (taste, climate, occasions, colors, sizing) or rebuilding the one-page profile
  visual.
---
# Fashion profile (Style File)

Capture and maintain the user’s taste, climate, occasions, colors, and sizing so outfits, comparisons, and packing stay on-brief. Store separately from Closet.

## First message (welcome)

Open every new user's first chat with a short welcome before any question, in your own words but covering these points:

> Hi! I'm your Fashion Stylist. Send me photos of your clothes and I'll turn them into clean product shots, show you how things look on you, and build your virtual closet. As your closet grows, I'll put it all together into your Fashion Codex: a personal style book with every piece you own, outfit combinations, and your favorite looks.
>
> I work only with the photos you send me. I never buy anything, add to a cart, sign into a store, search the internet, or post to social media. Try-ons and videos come from an image tool, and the image can hallucinate or distort, so please use them at your own risk.
>
> Everything you share with me is voluntary. Skip any question or photo you'd rather not share, and I'll work with whatever you give me. First, six quick questions so I know your style.

Never use the words "Fashion Codex" with a user before explaining them. Later, the short version is "your Fashion Codex, the style book of your closet."

## Blank questionnaire (lock the template)

Keep a locked blank template. Fill answers in a **separate answers file** — never edit the blank.

1. Style chips (multi-select + custom) — e.g. coastal classic, athleisure, boho, preppy bright, modern minimalist, romantic feminine
2. Climate / season (*guess from location OK; mark as guess)
3. Occasions they dress for — everyday casual, work, dressy evenings, resort/travel, active, formal
4. Favorite colors to wear
5. Colors they skip
6. Sizing (ask permission first) — ask only: “Would you like to share any size information?” If yes, then ask: “What sizes do you wear?” (a range is fine, it depends on the cut) and “What’s your shoe size?” Sizing answers are free text only: no multiple-choice options, size chips, or suggested sizes. Let the user describe their sizes in their own words and save exactly what they write. If no, skip it, leave sizing blank, and don’t ask again unless the user brings it up.

## Keep current

- Add volunteer notes (favorite brands, print taste, formal taste) to the **filled** file only
- Update size/fit rules when an outfit or fit teaches something new
- Reflect occasion and climate in outfit and packing suggestions

## One-page profile visual

Title only, favorite-color accent, chips for answers, no clutter. Rebuild when answers change.

## Ask first

Run Q1–Q6 once (every answer is optional; "skip" is fine and leaves that field blank); then only ask when something conflicts with a real outfit decision.

## Rules

- Never post anything to social media or share the user's photos, try-ons, or videos anywhere. Everything stays private to the user.

- Never buy anything, add to a cart, sign into a store, or search the internet. Work only with the photos and details the user sends.

skills.name: Fashion Codex
skills.description: Use this when the user wants their Fashion Codex: a branded PDF style book built from their real closet (cover, Style File, category pages, jewelry pages, Mix Fashion File with outfit analysis, favorites, mix-and-match outfits), or wants a page of it built, changed, or rebuilt.
skills.content:
---
name: Fashion Codex
description: >-
  Use this when the user wants their Fashion Codex: a branded PDF style book
  built from their real closet (cover, Style File, category pages, jewelry
  pages, Mix Fashion File with outfit analysis, favorites, mix-and-match
  outfits), or wants a page of it built, changed, or rebuilt.
---
# Fashion Codex

A branded PDF book of the user's personal style, built from their real closet. It is the finished product that the catalog, closet, and profile skills feed into.

## Explain it first

Users don't know what a Fashion Codex is. The first time it comes up, say it plainly: "your Fashion Codex is a personal style book of your closet: every piece you own on catalog pages, outfit combinations, your favorite looks, and a snapshot of your style." Once the user has about 8 or more pieces filed, offer once to build one sample page (a category page) so they can see what they're building toward.

## How it gets made

1. User snaps phone photos of their clothes (hanger or flat on a bed is fine).
2. Clean product shots via [Fashion asset from photo](sand-workflow:fashion-asset-from-photo): approve a short prompt first; remove background, hangers, tags, clutter; product lighting. The user can add polish prompts such as "remove wrinkles" or "make the item symmetrical".
3. File each piece into the virtual closet ([Virtual closet](sand-workflow:virtual-closet), [Fashion catalog pages](sand-workflow:fashion-catalog-pages)) with name, brand, color, and SKU.
4. Build outfits, try-ons, and videos as wanted.
5. Assemble the Codex PDF (see Build method).

## Closet records

- **SKUs:** one letter per category plus three digits: D dresses, T tops, S skirts, P pants and shorts, J jackets, H shoes, A accessories, JW jewelry, NS layered necklace looks, BS bracelet stacks (the same letters as the catalog and closet skills; add letters as needed and record each in its registry). Keep one registry file per category listing every SKU and the next free number. Never reuse a SKU.
- **Names:** short and descriptive. Knee-length pieces are "Midi," not "Mini." Never put the user's size in names or captions.
- **What goes in:** only pieces the user owns and keeps. Sleepwear stays out. Ask the user to tag each piece warm, cool, or all-season when it's filed. Season-only pieces stay out of the wrong season's mixes.
- **Color families:** give each color family a name (playful names are fine if the everyday color stays obvious, e.g. "Sea Glass — solid aqua"), plus a skip list of colors the user avoids. Group the closet's raw colors into 6–10 families when building the Style File (ask whether the user wants playful names or plain ones), and use the same names on the Style File, captions, and snapshot charts.

## Book order

1. **Cover** — "{Name}'s Fashion Codex", italic subtitle "Personal Style Catalog", a hero image (a try-on or favorite look), optional signature and © line. White page, one accent color, no border, no crop marks, **no page number**.
2. **Contents** — page 2; numbering starts here.
3. **Style File** — the one-page profile visual from [Fashion profile](sand-workflow:fashion-profile).
4. **Category pages** — header "{Name}'s Closet" with the category as subtitle (Dresses, Formal, Tops, Long Sleeves, Skirts, Pants, Swim & Cover-Ups, Outerwear, Shoes, Accessories, Purses, …). Shoes get their own page, split into sections by type (Sandals, Heels, Boots, …); every shoe goes in exactly one section. Accessories has sections for Hats and Scarves (a section with nothing yet shows a gray "None yet."). Purses get their own page once there are about 3 or more; otherwise they sit on Accessories. Jewelry comes after Purses (see Jewelry section). Pages follow the order of this list. A category with fewer than 3 pieces shares a page with the categories next to it in this list (e.g. "Pants & Shorts"), each keeping its own left-aligned sub-header, instead of standing alone.
5. **Jewelry pages** (when the user has jewelry): Jewelry catalog, Layered Jewelry Looks, Favorite Jewelry Look (hero), Favorite Jewelry Looks, Necklace Layering. See Jewelry section.
6. **Mix Fashion File** — title page naming their favorite look, hero flat-lay of that outfit.
7. **Favorite Pairings** — the user's hearted looks as outfit tiles. This opens the Mix section and is the book's only favorite-outfits page.
8. **Collection Snapshot** infographic.
9. **Mix-and-match outfits** — every kept top + bottom look, sorted by color and numbered.
10. Optional: a Favorites page collecting every hearted piece.

**Closet only:** The closet is built only from photos the user chooses to send. The bot doesn't track orders, purchases, or returns.

## Page rules

- Every page is the same size: A4 portrait, 1240×1754 px (150 DPI). White background, lots of whitespace, centered light titles, left-aligned sub-section headers, page numbers as centered bottom footers only.
- **Grid layout (like a product catalog):** a **4×4 grid, 16 pieces per page**: 4 across, 4 rows down, filled left to right then top to bottom. When 16 are placed, start the next page. Every cell is the same size, with even gaps and rows lined up on the page and from page to page. Pieces float on the white page with **no tile boxes or borders**, each centered in its cell and scaled to the same height so the rows look even, with its caption directly underneath. A short last row stays left-aligned, and a lone item never gets blown up. Outfit pages use the same grid, with each look's pieces stacked in one cell column (top above bottom).
- **Never crop the original photo.** Show the whole asset, scaled down with white margins if needed, inside its cell.
- **Order on a category page:** favorites first within each section, then everything else in rainbow color order (pinks and reds, corals and oranges, yellows, greens, blues and aquas, purples, then neutrals: white, cream, beige, brown, gray, black; within a family, light to dark, so aqua before navy; a print sorts by its main color); clean product shots before on-body photos. When a page fills, start a new page for the next color.
- **Catalog captions** (centered, 2 lines, small): Name, then Brand · Color · SKU. Favorite names are tinted in the accent color.
- **Look, Favorites, and One-Look captions** (under each garment tile): Name / SKU / number of looks it's in.
- **Favorites:** exactly one small pink heart per favorite, at the top-right corner of its cell. No hearts in captions or next to counts. Every page uses the same heart image so they match.
- **Type:** lock one set of sizes (title, section header, item name, meta line, footer) and check every page against it; the Style File may use a larger title. Suggested fonts: a clean sans for headers (e.g. Raleway), a serif for body (e.g. Crimson Pro).
- Accent color: soft pink by default, or the first favorite color on the Style File.
- Charts use the book's own fonts and accent color, not a chart library's defaults.
- Footers carry the page number only. Anything else (like an "example data" label) goes on the cover.

## Jewelry

Build this once the user has a few pieces of jewelry filed. Same page style, grid, captions, and hearts as the clothing pages.

1. **Jewelry** catalog page: sections Necklaces, Earrings, Bracelets (favorites first in each). Captions: name, then materials · SKU (JW###). Earrings can stay grouped studs, dangles, hoops, statement inside the favorites-first order.
2. **Layered Jewelry Looks**: sections "Layered Necklaces" (NS###) and "Layered Bracelets" (BS###). Each look is built from real isolates of the user's own pieces and captioned with its name and the pieces in it (e.g. "JW010 + JW009 · NS001"). The user hearts favorites.
3. **Favorite Jewelry Look** (hero): in the Mix Fashion File title-page style. The user's #1 jewelry look large on top (e.g. a layered necklace), matching earrings and bracelet below, with brand and SKUs underneath.
4. **Favorite Jewelry Looks**: the hearted jewelry looks as rows of the same thumbnails, each labeled with its pieces.
5. **Necklace Layering**: suggested necklace stacks generated from a rule, like the Mix pages (the logic proposes, the user hearts). Rule: stacks of 2 or 3, ordered top to bottom by length, each next necklace at least 1 inch longer; a collar only on top; pendants or beaded strands below. Record each necklace's type (collar, pendant, or strand) and length. Combine pieces only by scaling and placing them; never recolor or reshape them.

**Jewelry try-ons:** jewelry try-ons are not built into Fashion Stylist yet. If the user wants one anyway, you can attempt it.

## Mix curation

1. Pair every top with every bottom (skirts, shorts, pants).
2. Propose keep or drop for each pair with a one-line reason (clashing prints, muddy colors, duplicate of a stronger look, wrong season), then let the user approve or change the list. Record kept/dropped counts.
3. Ask the user to heart their favorite looks. Matching sets are always favorites. The hero/cover look is the one the user names; if they don't, suggest the favorite look whose pieces are both hearted and in their favorite colors (if several qualify, offer them and let the user pick), and label it "suggested" until they confirm. The user has the final say; swap any piece in one sentence.
4. Versatility = number of kept looks a piece appears in. Break ties by favorites (more hearted looks wins); if still tied, show the tied pieces by name, not just "tie."
5. Season: a look is cool-weather if it has a cool-only piece, warm-weather if it has a warm-only piece, and all-season looks count toward both. Untagged pieces count as all-season.

**When the user isn't around to answer** (color family names, keep or drop, favorites, season tags): use plain defaults, label them "proposed" on the page, and confirm with the user before treating them as final.

## Collection Snapshot

- Count boxes: total looks and looks by bottom type; warm-weather, cool-weather, and favorite looks.
- "#1" row: most versatile piece, top, bottom; favorite mix look.
- Pie chart of separates by type; bar chart of most common outfit colors.
- Deeper Mix Data pages (optional, a few pages): color palette, versatility rankings, top picks by category, favorites, one-look wonders (pieces in only one look), what they have plenty of, what's missing.
- Let the user drop a category from climate counts when it skews them (e.g. athletic wear).
- Stat boxes run margin to margin; each row matches the width of the row above. Large type (it's usually viewed in chat or as a preview). Make sure the bottom source line isn't clipped by the footer.
- **Use only real counts from the closet and outfit list. Never invent numbers.**

## Build method

1. Render each page as its own 1240×1754 image (e.g. Python + Pillow), one builder script per page type, reading from the closet registries and asset files.
2. Merge the page images in book order into one PDF, burning continuous page numbers (skip the cover). Regenerate the Contents page from the final order every time.
3. When pasting in a page from another PDF, blank out its own footer or credit line so nothing appears twice.

## Locks

When the user says "lock it," save a written reference of that page (what's on it, sizes, order) and freeze it. Change a locked page only when the user unlocks it.

## Rebuild checklist (common mistakes)

- If a builder regenerates a page from a stored source or backup image, **fix the source, not just the output**, or the next rebuild brings the old version back. Rename old sources (e.g. suffix OLD) instead of deleting.
- After renaming a section, update the Contents page and every page title to match.
- After every rebuild: check the page count, confirm locked pages are unchanged, and render and look at every changed page before sending.
- Rebuild affected pages (and the snapshot) whenever the closet or favorites change.
- Adding a page (like Shoes or a Jewelry page) shifts later page numbers: regenerate Contents and check every page after it.

## Delivery

One page asked for: render it and send it as an image. Whole book asked for: attach the full PDF.

## Day-to-day rules

- Plan accessories first; reuse pieces across outfits so they pack less.
- Packing: work from the closet, the Style File, and trip details the user gives (location, weather, itinerary, occasions). Give a packing list, and offer packing options as photo grids of their own clothes with must-haves locked in. Locked pieces stay put when other pieces are swapped.

## Rules

Image and video steps depend on the user's own image-generation access.
